ed_table01: Extended Data Table 1 | Experimental setup and noise threshold. Modality examples are actual outputs of the neutral Qwen3-4B teacher at stage 0, written as seed items → new items. The prompt templates of the other modalities have the same form, asking for eight new clusters or statements in the same style. τ is twice the median of the largest stage-0 difference among ten neutral system prompts (prompted) or eight null fine-tuned teachers (fine-tuned). Code has a high τ because neutral system prompts already disagree strongly there. Fine-tuned thresholds are 2 to 16 times higher because each fine-tuned teacher is a separately trained model, so a fine-tuned over-represented feature must be larger to count. A chain is capped at the stated number of stages; a length at the cap means at least that many links.
ed_table02: Extended Data Table 2 | One ban, all traits. Each ban set is the union of the bans two traits' chains had reached by stage 3 or 8 (raven and snail, chub and warbler on numbers; raven and snail on hexadecimal), applied to all eight teachers and the neutral teacher. The trait-specific excess is a teacher's excess minus the mean excess of the other seven teachers generated under the same ban, so shared responses to the ban cancel. Identification correlates a teacher's half-A pattern with every teacher's half-B pattern over the features the ban allows.
ed_table03: Extended Data Table 3 | Trait-specific component across chain stages. Cells are those with a stage-0 over-represented feature: for Qwen the 84 main cells plus 27 operator and code cells run at a lower threshold; stages are counted after the first ban. Direction and identity hold; size moves with the ban. In Qwen DNA and hexadecimal chains of 15–16 stages the direction drifts slowly with stage (lowest cosine 0.91 and 0.94; within-cell Spearman −0.89 to −0.92), and identity stays with the trait to the end.
ed_table04: Extended Data Table 4 | What each modality reads. Prompted teachers, Qwen3-4B, 28 animals and 60 traits with concept probes; the size-letter test also in Llama-3.2-3B.
ed_table05: Extended Data Table 5 | Prompted and fine-tuned teachers. The trait-specific part of the fine-tuning loss lies only in the name tokens, so cross-entropy rewards token identity and the last layers raise that logit directly. Origin layers are for 5 traits (prompted) and the 8 rare animals (fine-tuned). Over 60 traits the origin lies at one third to one half of the depth: prompted Qwen 4–19 and Llama 12–14, fine-tuned Qwen 13–17 and Llama 10–11.
ed_table06: Extended Data Table 6 | Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.2-3B. Both models have trait-specific retrieval heads, heads that read the answer text, spelling neurons and a shared relay; the differences come from the gains of those parts and from number tokenisation. Supplementary Table 9 gives the head- and neuron-level comparison. Head ablations used mean replacement, which understates head effects, so these drops are conservative; the 15-fold figure is for orange (chub 10-fold, raven 7-fold).
ed_table07: Extended Data Table 7 | What changing the data does to a student. Qwen3-4B, raven–snail, number modality. Transfer is the raven-student minus snail-student name margin with the standard error over datasets, one student per dataset and teacher. Against the unbanned condition on the same datasets, the four-feature ban removes 36% (3–70%, P = 0.036) and the fourteen-feature ban 74% (42–106%, P < 0.001), both against the 35-dataset baseline; the resampling conditions are compared with the 15-dataset baseline, which consists of the first 15 of the 35 datasets; the two resampling conditions differ from each other by +21% (−32 to +74, P = 0.41). The per-token log-likelihood ratio is the separation between the two teachers over the tokens of the dataset, relative to the unbanned condition, computed on the 15-dataset subset for every row. Ratios are point estimates against an estimated baseline, not intervals for the condition itself. Under both bans the transfer itself stays above zero (P < 0.001 and P = 0.021), so the bans reduce it without closing it. Every dataset holds 3,072 answers per teacher; in every condition 99.9–100% of answers are digits and separators only and none contains the name or a three-letter fragment of it, and under the bans answers are more varied (76–78% distinct, against 61% without a ban).
ed_table08: Extended Data Table 8 | One intervention, from the circuit to the student. Qwen3-4B, raven–snail, number modality. Relay and identity heads share four heads, so the union is 20, the size of the random control; the random set spans the same layers and is disjoint from the targeted ones. Teacher-side columns are measured on 12,288 answers per teacher per half; the contrast is the part of the raven − snail difference that replicates across the two halves. Students were trained on the teachers' unbanned number lists, so the name-leak column reads the same patch on the teacher side rather than the data the students saw; it is the share of answers that contain the name, not the share of list items used in Fig. 2. Student transfer is the raven-student minus snail-student name margin, one student per generated dataset over 35 datasets with one student seed each, and the error is the standard error over datasets; percentages are the paired difference from the random patch, divided by the unpatched mean transfer, with 95% confidence intervals and P values from a paired t test over the 35 datasets. The patched teachers' datasets keep the form of the unpatched ones (digits and separators only in 99.9% of answers, no name or fragment, 52.9 against 52.8 characters, 72% against 75% in the exact eleven-number format, 59–60% against 61% distinct answers), so the fall in transfer is not explained by gross changes in output format, length or diversity.
si_table01: Supplementary Table 1 | Composition of links by stage. Links are ordered by the stage at which they were banned. Restricted to the same cells, those with chains of at least 7 links, stages 1–3 are still 79–88% shared, so the late composition is not a survivor effect. Existing trait-specific tendencies make up only 2–7% of links in the rare-animal chains on numbers, DNA and hexadecimal.
si_table02: Supplementary Table 2 | Why modalities differ. A cell without a chain is not a cell without a trait effect: the shift is spread over many features and none crosses τ.
si_table03: Supplementary Table 3 | The leakage channels in words. Actual outputs of the Qwen snail teacher under each ban (numbers modality). Once every digit is banned the teacher often continues in Chinese prose; the Chinese is quoted as written, with an English translation in parentheses, and the Latin-script name or fragment inside it is the channel. Across all traits the excess moves to name fragments, not to words of related meaning, but prose like the last example shows that the trait can resurface as description.
si_table04: Supplementary Table 4 | Meaning in channels that are not names. Name fragments (any three letters of the trait name) were removed. The snail–slug pair shares its first letter, so spelling contributes there; loris–quoll and finch–warbler share none.
si_table05: Supplementary Table 5 | Same question, same random draws. The first six new numbers from prompted Qwen3-4B teachers that share the sampler's random draws, so they part only where the trait tips a choice. The neutral teacher takes the high road on one question and the low road on another; the large animals tilt such choices up and the small, slow ones down. The examples are chosen where the teachers part; the average effect is the balance in Fig. 6a.
si_table06: Supplementary Table 6 | Scope of the circuit results.
si_table10: Supplementary Table 10 | Threshold sensitivity. τ is each induction method's own threshold (Extended Data Table 1). The largest difference is taken over all features on half B without the z criterion, so it is an upper bound on what a chain could use. Prompted trait cells separate from their nulls from 0.5 to 3 τ; fine-tuned trait cells do not separate from fine-tuned nulls anywhere in this range.
si_table11: Supplementary Table 11 | All 28 animals. The balance is the share of newly generated three-digit numbers of 700 and above minus the share below 300, for the trait teacher minus the neutral teacher on the same questions; the expected first digit is the model's expected first digit of a new item, trait minus neutral, on shared neutral text. The eight animals of the main experiments were generated with 6,144 fresh questions per half, the other twenty with 64 questions answered 48 times, and the correlations hold within each group (weight +0.58 and +0.48, speed +0.67 and +0.50). Weight is a typical adult mass and speed the fastest mode of locomotion, a dive for the falcon and swimming for the whale and the dolphin.
